- _OUTLOOK: Draft a fully-formatted email into Outlook for Mac — opens a ready-to-review compose window, never sends. Drives classic Outlook via AppleScript with HTML content so paragraphs, bullet lists, and numbered lists render correctly; degrades to a plain-text mailto draft if only New Outlook is present. Pulls recipient addresses from CONTACTS.md and writes in Nick's email voice. USE WHEN draft an email, write an email to X, email X about Y, open a draft in Outlook, compose an email, reply to X, send an email (draft it for review). NOT FOR actually transmitting mail unattended (this is draft-only), Gmail/web mail (no Outlook desktop), or bulk/broadcast sends (use _BROADCAST). Mac only — requires osascript.
- Agents: Compose CUSTOM agents from Base Traits + Voice + Specialization, and manage predefined functional TEAMS. Traits combine expertise (security, technical, research), personality (skeptical, analytical, enthusiastic), and approach (thorough, rapid, systematic). ComposeAgent.ts merges base + user config, outputs unique prompt + ElevenLabs voice + prosody. Predefined teams: engineering, architecture, marketing, design, security, research, content, strategy — each YAML-configured with roles, tensions, and specialist members. Observer team variant: read-only oversight agents that vote continue/halt/escalate against the tool-activity audit log (high-blast-radius or unattended runs only). USE WHEN create custom agents, spin up agents, specialized agents, agent personalities, available traits, list traits, agent voices, compose agent, spawn parallel agents, launch agents, engineering team, architecture team, marketing team, design team, security team, research team, content team, strategy team, get the team on this, observer team, audit agents. NOT FOR ad-hoc swarms or TeamCreate coordination (use Delegation). NOT FOR single-threaded delegation without unique identities (use Delegation Task).
- ApertureOscillation: 3-pass scope oscillation that holds a question constant while shifting the scope envelope — narrow/tactical, wide/strategic, then synthesis — to surface design tensions invisible at any single zoom level. Requires two distinct inputs: the tactical target (what you're building) and strategic context (the larger system it serves). Pass 1 captures the component's own internal logic. Pass 2 reveals what the system needs it to be. Pass 3 finds where those views diverge — that delta is the output. Produces: design tensions, scope recommendations, and coherence assessments. Single workflow: Workflows/Oscillate.md. BPE-fragile — quarterly test recommended to verify smarter models don't naturally oscillate scope without prompting. Best integration point: Algorithm OBSERVE phase (before ISC) or THINK phase (before approach commitment). NOT a lens rotation (that's IterativeDepth) and NOT idea generation (that's BeCreative). NOT FOR deep incident causal chains (use RootCauseAnalysis) or assumption decomposition (use FirstPrinciples). USE WHEN aperture oscillation, oscillate scope, zoom in and out, tactical vs strategic, scope framing, design tension, architecture decision, feature fits system, system coherence check, local vs global design, build this inside that, wrong scope, design review, scope negotiation.
- Aphorisms: Manages a curated aphorism collection with full CRUD — content-based matching, themed search, thinker research, and database maintenance. Organizes quotes by author, theme, context, and newsletter usage history to prevent repetition. Four workflows: FindAphorism (analyze newsletter content, match themes, return 3-5 ranked recommendations with rationale), AddAphorism (parse quote + author, extract themes, validate uniqueness, update theme index), ResearchThinker (deep research on philosopher, add sourced quotes to database), SearchAphorisms (search by theme, keyword, or author). Database at ~/.claude/skills/aphorisms/Database/aphorisms.md — stores full quote text, author attribution, theme tags, context/background, source reference, and usage history per entry. Theme index supports 12+ categories: Work Ethic, Resilience, Learning, Stoicism, Risk, Wisdom, Truth-seeking, Excellence, Curiosity, Freedom, Rationality, Clarity. Supported thinkers: Hitchens, Feynman, Deutsch, Sam Harris, Spinoza, plus any requested author. Newsletter integration: tracks which quotes used in which issues to enforce variety; content theme extraction drives automated matching. USE WHEN: aphorism, quote, saying, find a quote, research thinker, add aphorism, search aphorisms, quote for newsletter, what did X say about, quotes about [topic], quote bank, find matching quote, quote collection, add this quote, check usage history. NOT FOR general creative writing or social media post generation — those go through dedicated writing/social skill…
- Apify: Scrape social media platforms, business data, and e-commerce via Apify actors — Instagram profiles/posts/hashtags/comments, LinkedIn profiles/jobs/posts, TikTok profiles/hashtags/videos/comments, YouTube channels/search/comments, Facebook posts/groups/comments, Google Maps business search with contact/review/image extraction, Amazon products/reviews/pricing, and general-purpose multi-page web crawling with custom pageFunction extraction logic. File-based TypeScript wrappers (scrapeInstagramProfile, searchGoogleMaps, scrapeAmazonProduct, scrapeWebsite, etc.) filter and transform data in code before returning to model context, achieving 95-99% token savings over direct MCP protocol. Parallel multi-platform queries via Promise.all for social listening dashboards. Lead enrichment pipeline: Google Maps → qualified filter → optional LinkedIn enrichment. Competitive analysis across Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok simultaneously. USE WHEN scrape Instagram, scrape LinkedIn, scrape TikTok, scrape YouTube, scrape Facebook, Google Maps leads, Amazon reviews, business intelligence, multi-platform social listening, competitive analysis, lead generation, social monitoring, Apify actors, web crawl, extract contacts. NOT FOR X/Twitter bookmarks (use a dedicated X-API skill) or progressive scraping (use BrightData).
- Art: Generates static visual content across 20+ formats via Flux, Nano Banana Pro (Gemini 3 Pro), and GPT-Image-1. Covers blog header illustrations, editorial art, Mermaid flowcharts, technical architecture diagrams, D3.js dashboards, taxonomies, timelines, 2x2 framework matrices, comparisons, annotated screenshots, recipe cards, aphorism/quote cards, conceptual maps, stat cards, comic panels, YouTube thumbnails, PAI pack icons, and brand-logo wallpapers. Named workflows: Essay, D3Dashboards, Visualize, Mermaid, TechnicalDiagrams, Taxonomies, Timelines, Frameworks, Comparisons, AnnotatedScreenshots, RecipeCards, Aphorisms, Maps, Stats, Comics, YouTubeThumbnailChecklist, AdHocYouTubeThumbnail, CreatePAIPackIcon, LogoWallpaper, RemoveBackground. SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS loads PREFERENCES.md, CharacterSpecs.md, and SceneConstruction.md. --remove-bg flag produces transparent-background PNG (can produce black backgrounds — verify visually). Up to 14 reference images per request (5 human, 6 object Gemini API limit). Output staged to ~/Downloads/ for preview before any project directory copy. Nano Banana Pro uses --size for resolution tier 1K/2K/4K and separate --aspect-ratio. USE WHEN: art, illustration, diagram, flowchart, infographic, header image, thumbnail, visualize, generate image, mermaid, architecture diagram, comic, icon, blog art, framework diagram, D3 chart, remove background, wallpaper. NOT FOR video or animation (use Remotion). NOT FOR the user's personal portrait/headshot (use a dedicated headshot skill).
- ArXiv: Search and retrieve arXiv academic papers by topic, category, or paper ID — with AlphaXiv-enriched AI-generated overviews. Uses arXiv Atom API (no auth) for discovery and search across cs.AI, cs.LG, cs.CL (NLP/LLMs), cs.CR (security), cs.MA (multi-agent), cs.SE, and cs.IR. Supports title (ti:), abstract (abs:), author (au:), and category (cat:) search fields with boolean operators (AND, OR, ANDNOT); sorts by lastUpdatedDate or relevance; paginates up to 2,000 results per call with 3s rate limit between calls. AlphaXiv enrichment fetches markdown summaries from alphaxiv.org/overview/{ID}.md; full text from alphaxiv.org/abs/{ID}.md as fallback; 404 means summary not yet generated. Workflows: Latest (new papers by category), Search (topic/keyword search), Paper (single paper deep-dive by ID or URL). API returns Atom XML — parse with text processing, not jq. HTTPS required with -L flag; check published date not lastUpdatedDate for truly new submissions. Output: paper title, authors, abstract, AlphaXiv summary, and direct arXiv URL. USE WHEN arxiv, papers, latest papers, research papers, new papers, what's new in AI research, recent ML papers, paper lookup, arxiv search, find paper by ID, summarize paper, latest NLP research, latest LLM papers, multi-agent papers, cs.AI latest, AI safety papers, software engineering papers, information retrieval papers. NOT FOR general web research (use Research), extracting content from arbitrary URLs (use Parser), or cybersecurity annual report analysis (use AnnualReports).
- AudioEditor: AI-powered audio and video editing pipeline: Whisper word-level transcription (insanely-fast-whisper on MPS) → Claude segment classification (KEEP / CUT_FILLER / CUT_FALSE_START / CUT_STUTTER / CUT_DEAD_AIR / CUT_EDIT_MARKER) → ffmpeg execution with 40ms qsin crossfades and room-tone gap fill → optional Cleanvoice API cloud polish for mouth sounds and loudness normalization. Distinguishes rhetorical pauses from accidental ones. Breaths attenuated to 50% volume (not removed). Preview mode (--preview flag) shows proposed cuts without modifying audio. Aggressive mode (--aggressive flag) applies tighter filler detection thresholds. Polish step (--polish flag) uploads to Cleanvoice API for mouth sound removal and loudness normalization — confirm before cloud upload of sensitive content. Pipeline tools: Transcribe.ts, Analyze.ts, Edit.ts, Polish.ts, Pipeline.ts. Single workflow: Clean.md. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; CLEANVOICE_API_KEY optional for polish step. USE WHEN: clean audio, edit audio, remove filler words, clean podcast, remove ums, cut dead air, polish audio, trim recording, audio cleanup, cut stutters, edit interview recording, preview edits, aggressive clean. NOT FOR video composition or animation (use Remotion).
- BeCreative
- BitterPillEngineering
- BrightData
- Browser: Headless browser automation via agent-browser — Rust CLI daemon with persistent auth profiles for fast, scriptable, parallel browser work. Supports batch commands, network interception, device emulation, per-site profile auth (one-time headed login, headless forever after), and parallel isolated sessions via --session. Workflows: ReviewStories (fan out YAML user stories to parallel UIReviewers), Automate (load/run parameterized recipe templates), Update. ## How the Hall of Fame case is framed

This is a **team** nomination (Hall of Fame inducts individuals or teams of members), under the **Surf Lifesaving** category. The team: Dr David Reid, Dr Katie Dixon, Chris Jacobson, Tracey Hare-Boyd, Dr Ned Douglas, Dr Leesa Equid.

The one criterion a panel will test is *"sustained excellence over a long period."* The nomination answers it directly: it attaches to the **team's careers in the category**, not the project's calendar age. These members carry a long body of work in the SLSA national Medical Advisory Group and the CPR curriculum, and the form expressly asks that "the complete career of the nominee is put forward." Lifesaving CPR is the culmination of that, and its impact is lasting (a first-of-its-kind national standard that will keep saving lives). The category explicitly lists "major innovations," the "international role in the saving of lives," and **Advisors** as eligible. Full case in file 02.

## How the two nominations connect

Chris Jacobson **introducing Lifesaving CPR** is the marquee proof point for his Life Membership case: the interpretive guidelines literally cite *"the introduction of CPR"* as the kind of distinguished contribution that qualifies, against which *"a patrol captain for 20 years would not of itself qualify."* So keep the two cases separate but mutually reinforcing: Chris's individual distinguished-service case (Life Membership), and the initiative's case (the team Hall of Fame nomination). **Both:** L-CPR wording resolved (2026-07-07): both nominations use the canonical phrasing from the Australian Honours nomination for Chris, "the first nationally coordinated CPR quality improvement initiative implemented by a community first aid organisation in Australia".

## Producing the upload documents

>
> In NSW he has also served in state emergency management roles at the Age and Open Championships (Deputy State Emergency Management Coordinator 2022/23; State Emergency Management Officer 2023/24), and his blended learning work was highly commended at the 2020 Australian Institute of Training & Development Excellence Awards. # SLSA Honours & Awards 2026: nomination pack

Two nominations, drafted from the SLSA forms, interpretive guidelines and bulletin, plus the Lifesaving CPR project materials.

**Source artefacts (filed 2026-06-23):** the F38 Hall of Fame nomination form, the 23-24 SLSA Honours bulletin, and the Interpretive Guidelines for SLSA Honours Awards 2022 now live in `~/OneDrive/06_Lifesaving/SLSA/2026/Honours-Nominations/`. The Lifesaving CPR substantiating evidence (6 Aims flyer, skills-maintenance session plan, skills-maintenance PowerPoint) is in that folder's `Supporting-Evidence-CPR/` subfolder. They were triaged out of `00_Inbox` into this nomination's permanent home.

## What's here

| File | Nomination | Status |
|------|-----------|--------|
| `01-life-membership-chris-jacobson.md` | **Life Membership: Chris Jacobson** | Full draft, field-by-field, within all character limits. High-confidence case. |
| `02-hall-of-fame-lifesaving-cpr.md` | **Hall of Fame: the Lifesaving CPR Team** | Committed team nomination under Surf Lifesaving. Draft complete; needs member details + endorsement. |

## How the Hall of Fame case is framed

This is a **team** nomination (Hall of Fame inducts individuals or teams of members), under the **Surf Lifesaving** category. The team: Dr David Reid, Dr Katie Dixon, Chris Jacobson, Tracey Hare-Boyd, Dr Ned Douglas, Dr Leesa Equid.

The one criterion a panel will test is *"sustained excellence over a long period."* The nomination answers it directly: it attaches to the **team's careers in the category**, not the project's calendar age. These members carry a long body of work in the SLSA national Medical Advisory Group and the CPR curriculum, and the form expressly asks that "the complete career of the nominee is put forward." Lifesaving CPR is the culmination of that, and its impact is lasting (a first-of-its-kind national standard that will keep saving lives). The category explicitly lists "major innovations," the "international role in the saving of lives," and **Advisors** as eligible. Full case in file 02.

## How the two nominations connect

Chris Jacobson **introducing Lifesaving CPR** is the marquee proof point for his Life Membership case: the interpretive guidelines literally cite *"the introduction of CPR"* as the kind of distinguished contribution that qualifies, against which *"a patrol captain for 20 years would not of itself qualify."* So keep the two cases separate but mutually reinforcing: Chris's individual distinguished-service case (Life Membership), and the initiative's case (the team Hall of Fame nomination). Do not run Chris individually for the Hall of Fame as well; it would dilute both.

## Key dates and rules

- **Life Membership (SLSA Honours):** online Jotform only; deadlines **25 January** and **18 July**. Must be nominated by the President or two (2) SLSA members. Re-nomination allowed after 2 years if unsuccessful.
- **Hall of Fame:** club-endorsed, forwarded to **honours@slsa.asn.au**; considered twice yearly. Re-submission after 2 years if not endorsed.

## Consolidated "you supply" list

**Chris Jacobson (Life Membership):** Member ID · DOB · address · mobile · email · proposer & seconder (or President) · photo · Surfguard printout · letters of recommendation (confirmed: Peter Agnew, SLSA President; Tony van den Enden, SLST CEO; Lyn Barratt, SLSA Life Member). Clubs: Ulverstone SLSC 2004-present (continuing) and Elouera SLSC 2022-present (current primary). Still to confirm: exact SLSNSW emergency-management titles.

**Lifesaving CPR Team (Hall of Fame):** per-member Member IDs + clubs + a short note on each member's years of MAG / CPR-curriculum service · point-of-contact details · club endorsement (name, position, signature, date) · team/initiative photo · outcome evidence (members trained, pilot results, international recognition, clinical endorsement).

**Both:** L-CPR wording resolved (2026-07-07): both nominations use the canonical phrasing from the Australian Honours nomination for Chris, "the first nationally coordinated CPR quality improvement initiative implemented by a community first aid organisation in Australia".

## Producing the upload documents

The Records of Service and the 2-page conclusive history are drafted in markdown here. When ready, render them to PDF/Word for upload (do not put the markdown source into OneDrive; export the rendered artefact to the OneDrive destination).

Chris has spent twenty years advancing surf lifesaving at the national level, and Australian lifesavers train, patrol and resuscitate differently because of it. His national service began at the 2006 SLSA Youth Development Forum and has continued without pause ever since. He served fourteen years on the Lifesaving Members Advisory Committee (2012-2025), nine of them as National Chair of Lifesaving (2016-2025), alongside twelve years on the National Meritorious Awards Committee, which he chaired from 2017 to 2024.

As National Chair he reshaped how every Australian lifesaver is trained. He chaired the 2019 National Lifesaving Curriculum Review, chaired the rewrite of the Public Safety and Aquatic Rescue manual and produced its first online interactive edition, built the first nationally delivered blended learning model for the Surf Rescue Certificate and Bronze Medallion, and chaired three national course redesigns (Bronze Medallion, Silver Medallion Aquatic Rescue and Silver Medallion Patrol Captain). That body of work earned an international award for best use of blended learning in 2020.

He then looked to the future. He founded and facilitated SLSA's inaugural National Innovation Day (2024), founded and chaired the Expanding Horizons Review (2024), and served as National Implementation Lead for Lifesaving CPR (2024-2026), the first nationally coordinated CPR quality improvement initiative implemented by a community first aid organisation in Australia, personally leading the national roadshow that upskilled trainers around the country.

His contribution is conspicuous as well as distinguished. He was named SLSA Australian Surf Lifesaver of the Year in 2011/12, the youngest ever recipient and the only Tasmanian recipient, and holds the International Life Saving Federation Citation of Merit. Through all of it he has remained a frontline volunteer, patrolling every season since 2004 across Ulverstone and Elouera SLSCs, and his output is so far beyond what members expect of a volunteer that he is routinely mistaken for paid staff. Few members in the modern era have a contribution that is so national, so sustained and so directly attributable to one person.
EOF
cat > s7v2.txt <<'EOF'
Chris's club service is distinguished by leadership and education rather than tenure alone. He has patrolled for 22 unbroken seasons since joining Ulverstone SLSC in 2004, and he patrols still, now at Elouera SLSC in Sydney while remaining a continuing member of his home club. Sustained frontline service across two clubs and two states, without a single season's break, is itself uncommon. What makes it distinguished is what he built along the way.

As Patrol Captain for nine consecutive seasons (2007-2016) he carried frontline rescue responsibility on Ulverstone's beach. As Vice President, Lifesaving (2011) and Club Training Officer (2011-2013) he built the club's lifesaving operations and education capability, and from 2007 he has served continuously as a Trainer, Assessor and Facilitator, delivering award courses that began at club level and grew to branch, state and national delivery. These club roles were the foundation of everything that followed. The training systems he later rebuilt nationally were first learned, tested and taught on his own club's beach.

His peers recognised it twice, naming him Club Person of the Year in 2010/11 and again in 2011/12, back-to-back recognition across consecutive seasons. Beyond the formal roles, Chris remains the member every club officer knows they can call. He always takes the phone call, gives the advice, or helps with the project or problem in front of them, and he has done so for two decades.
EOF

At branch level Chris has consistently held the roles that carry real operational accountability for members and the public. As a Senior Duty Officer with SLS Sydney (2022-present) he is one of the people responsible for coordinating the branch's emergency lifesaving response, and he has served on the SLS Sydney Support Operations Team since 2020. That role builds directly on his earlier work in Tasmania, where he helped establish the Duty Officer function itself, authoring the training and standards the role still runs on.

His branch service began as Secretary of Tasmania's Regional Lifesaving Committee (2010-2012), and he has continued to assist at branch and regional level in every state he has lived in. That pattern is what makes his service significant. Chris is one of the few members who has carried operational lifesaving responsibility at club, branch, state and national level simultaneously, which means the national policy he writes is informed by the beach, and the branch operations he coordinates are informed by national direction. It has allowed him to roll out national policy and direction effectively while remaining genuinely involved at every level of the organisation, and it has been sustained for more than fifteen years across two states.
EOF

Chris's state service is distinguished by both its depth and the fact that it spans three states, with peer-judged excellence in every domain he has touched. In Tasmania he progressed from State Development Squad Captain (2005/06) and Under-19 Surf Life Saver of the Year (2007) through thirteen years on the State Emergency Response Team (2007-2020), the Awards of Excellence Panel (2009-2016), State Patrol Assessor (2010-2016) and State Duty Officer (2014-2020), to Chair of Lifesaving (2012-2016), the state's senior lifesaving position, before stepping up to the national chair. His signature state contribution is the Lifesaving Development Camp. Establishing the same member-development programme from scratch in three different states is a contribution directly and uniquely attributable to him.

In NSW he has also served in state emergency management roles at the Age and Open Championships, as Deputy State Emergency Management Coordinator in 2022/23 and State Emergency Management Officer in 2023/24, and his blended learning work was highly commended at the 2020 Australian Institute of Training & Development Excellence Awards. His peers have judged his service the best in the state across multiple domains, naming him SLST Volunteer of the Year (2010/11), Lifesaver of the Year (2011/12) and Trainer of the Year twice (2011/12 and 2018). And the service continues. Having moved interstate, he still serves Tasmania today on the SLST Operations Executive (2025-present). Two decades, three states, and counting.
EOF

He chaired the 2019 National Lifesaving Curriculum Review, chaired the rewrite of the Public Safety and Aquatic Rescue manual and delivered its first online interactive edition, built the first nationally delivered blended learning model for the Surf Rescue Certificate and Bronze Medallion, and chaired three national course redesigns (Bronze Medallion, Silver Medallion Aquatic Rescue and Silver Medallion Patrol Captain). The blended learning work won an international award in 2020. He founded and facilitated the inaugural National Innovation Day (2024) and founded and chaired the Expanding Horizons Review (2024). Each of these exists because Chris initiated it, argued for it and carried it.

Significant. This is not administration of an existing system but transformation of it. Every Surf Rescue Certificate, Bronze Medallion and Silver Medallion candidate in Australia now trains through models and manuals Chris built or rebuilt, and every club's resuscitation practice is being lifted by an initiative he led. Through twelve years on the National Meritorious Awards Committee (2013-2025), seven as Chair (2017-2024), he also shaped how SLSA recognises its own members, overseeing the Lifesaver of the Year and Volunteer of the Year awards and their judging panels, leading the 2021 review of the lifesaving award criteria and introducing the Youth Surf Life Saver of the Year award.

Sustained. His national service began at the 2006 SLSA Youth Development Forum, twenty years ago, and has continued without pause, as a national Trainer, Assessor and Facilitator since 2007, through the Silver Medallion Aquatic Rescue pilot in 2011, and across fourteen years on the Lifesaving Members Advisory Committee (2012-2025) with nine as National Chair.

Conspicuous. He was named SLSA Australian Surf Lifesaver of the Year in 2011/12, the youngest ever recipient and the only Tasmanian recipient. His efforts and initiatives have earned the praise of even his harshest critics, and his commitment and passion are so well known that members routinely mistake him for paid staff. He is, and has always been, a volunteer.

**[437 / 1000 words]**

> Chris is known across SLSA as the person who moves the organisation forward. His national service meets all three limbs of the Life Membership standard, with contributions that are unique and directly attributable to him rather than to any group he sat on.
>
> Distinguished. The interpretive guidelines for this award cite the introduction of CPR as the benchmark example of a distinguished contribution. Chris was the National Implementation Lead for Lifesaving CPR (2024-2026), the first nationally coordinated CPR quality improvement initiative implemented by a community first aid organisation in Australia, and he personally led the national roadshow that upskilled trainers around the country. Before that, as National Chair of Lifesaving (2016-2025) he reshaped how every Australian lifesaver is trained: he chaired the 2019 National Lifesaving Curriculum Review, chaired the rewrite of the Public Safety and Aquatic Rescue manual and delivered its first online interactive edition, built the first nationally delivered blended learning model for the Surf Rescue Certificate and Bronze Medallion, and chaired three national course redesigns (Bronze Medallion, Silver Medallion Aquatic Rescue and Silver Medallion Patrol Captain). The blended learning work won an international award in 2020. He founded and facilitated the inaugural National Innovation Day (2024) and founded and chaired the Expanding Horizons Review (2024). Each of these exists because Chris initiated it, argued for it and carried it.
>
> Significant. This is not administration of an existing system but transformation of it. Every Surf Rescue Certificate, Bronze Medallion and Silver Medallion candidate in Australia now trains through models and manuals Chris built or rebuilt, and every club's resuscitation practice is being lifted by an initiative he led. Through twelve years on the National Meritorious Awards Committee (2013-2025), seven as Chair (2017-2024), he also shaped how SLSA recognises its own members, overseeing the Lifesaver of the Year and Volunteer of the Year awards and their judging panels, leading the 2021 review of the lifesaving award criteria and introducing the Youth Surf Life Saver of the Year award.
>
> Sustained. His national service began at the 2006 SLSA Youth Development Forum, twenty years ago, and has continued without pause: national Trainer, Assessor and Facilitator since 2007, the Silver Medallion Aquatic Rescue pilot in 2011, fourteen years on the Lifesaving Members Advisory Committee (2012-2025) and nine as National Chair.
>
> Conspicuous. He was named SLSA Australian Surf Lifesaver of the Year in 2011/12, the youngest ever recipient and the only Tasmanian recipient. His efforts and initiatives have earned the praise of even his harshest critics, and his commitment and passion are so well known that members routinely mistake him for paid staff. He is, and has always been, a volunteer.

===== 260716 - Letter of Support CJ SLSA LM.pdf =====
16th July 2026

Letter of Support for Surf Life Saving Australia Life Membership - Christopher Jacobson
To the SLSA Honours Assessment Panel,
I would like to provide my strongest possible support for the nomination of Christopher Jacobson
for Life Membership of Surf Life Saving Australia (SLSA).
Life Membership is the highest honour that can be bestowed upon a member of our movement
and should be reserved for those whose service is distinguished, sustained, and has made an
exceptional contribution to Surf Life Saving Australia. In my view, Chris not only meets these criteria
but stands as one of the most significant volunteer contributors to the lifesaving movement of his
generation. His impact has been felt at club, branch, state, national and international levels over
more than twenty years of continuous service to surf life saving.
Chris commenced his active patrol service in 2004 at Ulverstone Surf Life Saving Club and remains
an active patrolling member today. Throughout that period he has served in numerous operational,
educational and leadership roles, including Patrol Captain, Club Training Officer, Vice President
Lifesaving, State Duty Officer, State Emergency Response Team member, Senior Duty Officer with
Surf Life Saving Sydney, Chair of Lifesaving for Surf Life Saving Tasmania, and most notably
National Chair of Lifesaving for Surf Life Saving Australia from 2016 to 2025.
What distinguishes Chris from many highly dedicated volunteers is the breadth of his influence and
the lasting legacy of his initiatives. As National Chair of Lifesaving, he became the youngest person
to hold the role and led some of the most important reforms in modern lifesaving history. He
chaired the National Lifesaving Curriculum Review, oversaw the redesign of the Bronze Medallion,
Surf Rescue Certificate and Silver Medallion pathways, and developed the first nationally delivered
blended learning model used across Australia. These reforms fundamentally changed how surf
lifesavers are trained and continue to influence the development of thousands of new members
each year.
Chris has consistently demonstrated an ability to identify future challenges and create innovative
solutions. He led the rewrite of the Public Safety Aquatic Rescue Manual, delivering the first
interactive online version, founded Surf Life Saving Australia's inaugural National Innovation Day,
and conceived the Expanding Horizons Review to address future volunteer and service delivery
challenges facing the movement. These initiatives have helped position SLSA as a contemporary,
forward-thinking emergency service organisation.
His leadership of the Lifesaving CPR (L-CPR) program represents another outstanding achievement.
As National Implementation Lead, Chris spearheaded the first nationally coordinated CPR quality
improvement initiative delivered by a community first aid organisation in Australia. The program

Importantly, Chris has never lost sight of grassroots lifesaving. Throughout his national service he
has remained actively engaged with clubs, branches and states, continuing to patrol, train, mentor
and support members. He has delivered award courses for nearly two decades and has personally
influenced the development of countless lifesavers, trainers, assessors, patrol captains and leaders
across Australia. His willingness to share knowledge, support emerging leaders and invest in others
has created a lasting multiplier effect across the organisation.
His achievements have been recognised repeatedly by his peers. He remains the youngest recipient
and only Tasmanian recipient of the Australian Surf Lifesaver of the Year Award, has received an
International Life Saving Federation Citation of Merit, and has been recognised through numerous
state and national awards for volunteerism, training and lifesaving excellence.
Beyond Australia, Chris has represented the movement with distinction through international
presentations, drowning prevention initiatives and water safety work overseas, helping share
Australian lifesaving expertise with the broader international community.
When assessing Life Membership nominations, consideration should be given not simply to years
of service, but to the significance, influence and enduring value of that service. Chris's contribution
satisfies all of these measures. His work has strengthened national capability, improved education
and operational standards, fostered innovation, enhanced public safety outcomes and shaped the
strategic direction of Surf Life Saving Australia for many years to come. Few volunteers can
demonstrate a comparable level of sustained leadership and national impact while remaining
committed to frontline volunteer service.
I therefore offer my unequivocal endorsement of Christopher Jacobson's nomination and
respectfully submit that he is an exceptionally worthy recipient of Life Membership of Surf Life
Saving Australia. His service epitomises the values, commitment and excellence that this honour is
intended to recognise.

Yours sincerely,

Tony van den Enden

an active patrolling member today. Throughout that period he has served in numerous operational,
educational and leadership roles, including Patrol Captain, Club Training Officer, Vice President
Lifesaving, State Duty Officer, State Emergency Response Team member, Senior Duty Officer with
Surf Life Saving Sydney, Chair of Lifesaving for Surf Life Saving Tasmania, and most notably
National Chair of Lifesaving for Surf Life Saving Australia from 2016 to 2025.
What distinguishes Chris from many highly dedicated volunteers is the breadth of his influence and
the lasting legacy of his initiatives. As National Chair of Lifesaving, he became the youngest person
to hold the role and led some of the most important reforms in modern lifesaving history. He
chaired the National Lifesaving Curriculum Review, oversaw the redesign of the Bronze Medallion,
Surf Rescue Certificate and Silver Medallion pathways, and developed the first nationally delivered
blended learning model used across Australia. These reforms fundamentally changed how surf
lifesavers are trained and continue to influence the development of thousands of new members
each year.
Chris has consistently demonstrated an ability to identify future challenges and create innovative
solutions. He led the rewrite of the Public Safety Aquatic Rescue Manual, delivering the first
interactive online version, founded Surf Life Saving Australia's inaugural National Innovation Day,
and conceived the Expanding Horizons Review to address future volunteer and service delivery
challenges facing the movement. These initiatives have helped position SLSA as a contemporary,
forward-thinking emergency service organisation.
His leadership of the Lifesaving CPR (L-CPR) program represents another outstanding achievement.
As National Implementation Lead, Chris spearheaded the first nationally coordinated CPR quality
improvement initiative delivered by a community first aid organisation in Australia. The program

has remained actively engaged with clubs, branches and states, continuing to patrol, train, mentor
and support members. He has delivered award courses for nearly two decades and has personally
influenced the development of countless lifesavers, trainers, assessors, patrol captains and leaders
across Australia. His willingness to share knowledge, support emerging leaders and invest in others
has created a lasting multiplier effect across the organisation.

and only Tasmanian recipient of the Australian Surf Lifesaver of the Year Award, has received an

Chris Jacobson's story is one of dedication that has never paused, from a young lifesaver joining Ulverstone SLSC in 2004 to one of the most influential volunteer leaders in modern Australian lifesaving. He stepped onto the national stage at the 2006 SLSA Youth Development Forum at the very start of his journey, and twenty years later he has never left it. By 2011/12 he was the SLSA Australian Surf Lifesaver of the Year, the youngest ever recipient and the only Tasmanian to receive the award. He went on to serve fourteen years on the Lifesaving Members Advisory Committee (2012-2025), and in 2016 became the youngest person to hold the role of National Chair of Lifesaving, which he held for nine years.

As National Chair he transformed how every Australian lifesaver is trained. He chaired the National Lifesaving Curriculum Review, chaired the rewrite of the Public Safety and Aquatic Rescue manual and delivered its first online interactive edition, chaired the redesign of the Bronze Medallion, Silver Medallion Aquatic Rescue and Silver Medallion Patrol Captain courses, and built the first nationally delivered blended learning model for the Surf Rescue Certificate and Bronze Medallion, work recognised with an international award for best use of blended learning in 2020. These reforms continue to shape the development of thousands of new members every year.

He has always looked to the movement's future. He founded the inaugural National Innovation Day, conceived and chaired the Expanding Horizons Review, now a core strategic project confronting the future volunteer and service delivery challenges facing the movement, and served as National Implementation Lead for Lifesaving CPR (2024-2026), the first nationally coordinated CPR quality improvement initiative implemented by a community first aid organisation in Australia. As Chair of the National Meritorious Awards Committee (2017-2024) he introduced the Youth Surf Life Saver of the Year award, ensuring the next generation is recognised as he once was.

Through all of it he has remained a frontline volunteer. He still patrols today at Elouera SLSC, remains a member and an asset to Ulverstone SLSC and Tasmania long after moving interstate, and gives so much of himself that members around the country routinely assume he is paid staff. He is not. He is a volunteer, and that is the measure of his dedication.
EOF
cat > s7v3.txt <<'EOF'
Chris joined Ulverstone SLSC in 2004 and has patrolled every season since, twenty-two unbroken years of frontline service that continues today at Elouera SLSC in Sydney. What makes his club service distinguished is not tenure alone but what he built along the way, and the fact that he has never really left. He remains a continuing member of Ulverstone and an ongoing asset to his home club long after moving interstate, still mentoring its members and still taking the phone call whenever the club needs advice or help with a project or a problem.

As Patrol Captain for nine consecutive seasons (2007-2016) he carried frontline rescue responsibility on Ulverstone's beach. As Vice President, Lifesaving (2011) and Club Training Officer (2011-2013) he built the club's lifesaving operations and education capability, and from 2007 he has served continuously as a Trainer, Assessor and Facilitator, delivering award courses that began at club level and grew to branch, state and national delivery. The training systems he later rebuilt for the whole country were first learned, tested and taught on his own club's beach, and the members he has trained and mentored across two decades are his most personal legacy.

His peers saw it early, naming him Club Person of the Year in 2010/11 and again in 2011/12, back-to-back recognition in consecutive seasons. Two decades on, the dedication has not dimmed. Chris remains the member every club officer knows they can call, at Ulverstone, at Elouera, and at clubs around the country.
EOF
cat > s9v3.txt <<'EOF'
Chris's state service tells a story few in the movement can match, and it spans three states. It begins in Tasmania, where he progressed from State Development Squad Captain (2005/06) and Under-19 Surf Life Saver of the Year (2007) through thirteen years on the State Emergency Response Team (2007-2020), the Awards of Excellence Panel (2009-2016), State Patrol Assessor (2010-2016) and State Duty Officer (2014-2020), to Chair of Lifesaving (2012-2016), the state's senior lifesaving position. As state Chair he authored Tasmania's Duty Officer training and standards and chaired the editorial panel that produced SLST's inaugural Standard Operating Procedures, documents the state's operations still stand on today.

His signature state contribution is the Lifesaving Development Camp. He coordinated Tasmania's inaugural camp and ran it for six years (2014-2020) as the state's most successful lifesaving development programme, then carried it personally into two more states, establishing the inaugural SLSQ camp in 2019 and the inaugural SLSNSW camps in 2021 and 2022. Building the same member development programme from scratch in three different states is a contribution directly and uniquely attributable to one person's dedication.

In NSW he has served in state emergency management roles at the Age and Open Championships, as Deputy State Emergency Management Coordinator in 2022/23 and State Emergency Management Officer in 2023/24, and his blended learning work was highly commended at the 2020 Australian Institute of Training and Development Excellence Awards. His peers have repeatedly judged his service the best in the state, naming him SLST Volunteer of the Year (2010/11), Lifesaver of the Year (2011/12) and Trainer of the Year twice (2011/12 and 2018).

Most telling of all is what happened after he left. Moving interstate usually ends a member's state service. Chris's never stopped. He continues to serve Tasmania today on the SLST Operations Executive (2025-present), still contributing to the state that shaped him years after he moved away. That is the pattern of his whole story, sustained dedication that outlasts geography. Two decades, three states, and counting.
EOF
cat > s10v3.txt <<'EOF'
Chris is known across SLSA as the person who moves the organisation forward, and his national record tells the story of a volunteer who kept showing up, kept innovating and kept lifting the standard for twenty years without pause. His service meets all three limbs of the Life Membership standard, with contributions that are unique and directly attributable to him rather than to any group he sat on.

Distinguished. The interpretive guidelines for this award cite the introduction of CPR as the benchmark example of a distinguished contribution. Chris was the National Implementation Lead for Lifesaving CPR (2024-2026), the first nationally coordinated CPR quality improvement initiative implemented by a community first aid organisation in Australia, personally leading the national roadshow that upskilled trainers around the country. That alone meets the benchmark, and it sits on top of a decade of national transformation. Appointed in 2016 as the youngest person to hold the role of National Chair of Lifesaving, he reshaped how every Australian lifesaver is trained. He chaired the 2019 National Lifesaving Curriculum Review, chaired the rewrite of the Public Safety and Aquatic Rescue manual and delivered its first online interactive edition, and chaired three national course redesigns across the Bronze Medallion, Silver Medallion Aquatic Rescue and Silver Medallion Patrol Captain. He built the first nationally delivered blended learning model for the Surf Rescue Certificate and Bronze Medallion, work whose quality was recognised beyond the movement with an international award for best use of blended learning in 2020 and a highly commended at the Australian Institute of Training and Development Excellence Awards. He founded and facilitated the inaugural National Innovation Day, and he conceived, founded and chaired the Expanding Horizons Review, which has become a core strategic project for the organisation, confronting the future volunteer and service delivery challenges facing the movement. Each of these initiatives exists because Chris saw the need, argued for it and carried it.

Significant. This is not the administration of an existing system but the transformation of it. Every Surf Rescue Certificate, Bronze Medallion and Silver Medallion candidate in Australia now trains through models and manuals Chris built or rebuilt, reforms that continue to shape the development of thousands of new members every year, and every club's resuscitation practice is being lifted by an initiative he led. Through twelve years on the National Meritorious Awards Committee (2013-2025), seven as Chair (2017-2024), he also shaped how SLSA recognises its own members, overseeing the Lifesaver of the Year and Volunteer of the Year awards and their judging panels, leading the 2021 review of the lifesaving award criteria and introducing the Youth Surf Life Saver of the Year award so that the next generation of standouts is recognised as he once was.

Sustained. His national service began at the 2006 SLSA Youth Development Forum, twenty years ago, and has never stopped. He has been a national Trainer, Assessor and Facilitator since 2007, piloted the Silver Medallion Aquatic Rescue in 2011, and served fourteen consecutive years on the Lifesaving Members Advisory Committee (2012-2025) with nine as National Chair. There is no gap in this record. Every season for two decades, Chris has been doing the work.

Conspicuous. He was named SLSA Australian Surf Lifesaver of the Year in 2011/12, the youngest ever recipient and the only Tasmanian recipient. His efforts have earned the praise of even his harshest critics, and the sheer volume and quality of his output is so far beyond what anyone expects of a volunteer that members around the country routinely assume he is paid staff. He is not, and never has been. Twenty years of that record, given freely, is the definition of conspicuous service.
EOF

> Chris's state service is distinguished by both its depth and the fact that it spans three states, with peer-judged excellence in every domain he has touched. In Tasmania he progressed from State Development Squad Captain (2005/06) and Under-19 Surf Life Saver of the Year (2007) through thirteen years on the State Emergency Response Team (2007-2020), the Awards of Excellence Panel (2009-2016), State Patrol Assessor (2010-2016) and State Duty Officer (2014-2020), to Chair of Lifesaving (2012-2016), the state's senior lifesaving position, before stepping up to the national chair. As state Chair he authored Tasmania's Duty Officer training and standards and chaired the editorial panel that produced SLST's inaugural Standard Operating Procedures, documents the state's operations still stand on.
>
> His signature state contribution is the Lifesaving Development Camp. He coordinated Tasmania's inaugural camp and ran it for six years (2014-2020) as the state's most successful lifesaving development programme, then carried it personally into two more states, coordinating the inaugural SLSQ camp in 2019 and the inaugural SLSNSW camps in 2021 and 2022. Establishing the same member-development programme from scratch in three different states is a contribution directly and uniquely attributable to him.
>
> In NSW he has also served in state emergency management roles at the Age and Open Championships, as Deputy State Emergency Management Coordinator in 2022/23 and State Emergency Management Officer in 2023/24, and his blended learning work was highly commended at the 2020 Australian Institute of Training & Development Excellence Awards. His peers have judged his service the best in the state across multiple domains, naming him SLST Volunteer of the Year (2010/11), Lifesaver of the Year (2011/12) and Trainer of the Year twice (2011/12 and 2018). And the service continues. Having moved interstate, he still serves Tasmania today on the SLST Operations Executive (2025-present). Two decades, three states, and counting.

>

> Chris is known across SLSA as the person who moves the organisation forward. His national service meets all three limbs of the Life Membership standard, with contributions that are unique and directly attributable to him rather than to any group he sat on.
>
> Distinguished. The interpretive guidelines for this award cite the introduction of CPR as the benchmark example of a distinguished contribution. Chris was the National Implementation Lead for Lifesaving CPR (2024-2026), the first nationally coordinated CPR quality improvement initiative implemented by a community first aid organisation in Australia, and he personally led the national roadshow that upskilled trainers around the country. Before that, as National Chair of Lifesaving (2016-2025) he reshaped how every Australian lifesaver is trained. He chaired the 2019 National Lifesaving Curriculum Review, chaired the rewrite of the Public Safety and Aquatic Rescue manual and delivered its first online interactive edition, built the first nationally delivered blended learning model for the Surf Rescue Certificate and Bronze Medallion, and chaired three national course redesigns (Bronze Medallion, Silver Medallion Aquatic Rescue and Silver Medallion Patrol Captain). The blended learning work won an international award in 2020. He founded and facilitated the inaugural National Innovation Day (2024) and founded and chaired the Expanding Horizons Review (2024). Each of these exists because Chris initiated it, argued for it and carried it.
>
> Significant. This is not administration of an existing system but transformation of it. Every Surf Rescue Certificate, Bronze Medallion and Silver Medallion candidate in Australia now trains through models and manuals Chris built or rebuilt, and every club's resuscitation practice is being lifted by an initiative he led. Through twelve years on the National Meritorious Awards Committee (2013-2025), seven as Chair (2017-2024), he also shaped how SLSA recognises its own members, overseeing the Lifesaver of the Year and Volunteer of the Year awards and their judging panels, leading the 2021 review of the lifesaving award criteria and introducing the Youth Surf Life Saver of the Year award.
>
> Sustained. His national service began at the 2006 SLSA Youth Development Forum, twenty years ago, and has continued without pause, as a national Trainer, Assessor and Facilitator since 2007, through the Silver Medallion Aquatic Rescue pilot in 2011, and across fourteen years on the Lifesaving Members Advisory Committee (2012-2025) with nine as National Chair.
>
> Conspicuous. He was named SLSA Australian Surf Lifesaver of the Year in 2011/12, the youngest ever recipient and the only Tasmanian recipient. His efforts and initiatives have earned the praise of even his harshest critics, and his commitment and passion are so well known that members routinely mistake him for paid staff. He is, and has always been, a volunteer.

>

Chris was the National Implementation Lead for Lifesaving CPR (2024-2026), the first nationally coordinated CPR quality improvement initiative implemented by a community first aid organisation in Australia, personally leading the national roadshow that upskilled trainers around the country. That alone meets the benchmark, and it sits on top of a decade of national transformation. Appointed in 2016 as the youngest person to hold the role of National Chair of Lifesaving, he reshaped how every Australian lifesaver is trained. He chaired the 2019 National Lifesaving Curriculum Review, chaired the rewrite of the Public Safety and Aquatic Rescue manual and delivered its first online interactive edition, and chaired three national course redesigns across the Bronze Medallion, Silver Medallion Aquatic Rescue and Silver Medallion Patrol Captain. He built the first nationally delivered blended learning model for the Surf Rescue Certificate and Bronze Medallion, work whose quality was recognised beyond the movement with an international award for best use of blended learning in 2020 and a highly commended at the Australian Institute of Training and Development Excellence Awards. He founded and facilitated the inaugural National Innovation Day, and he conceived, founded and chaired the Expanding Horizons Review, which has become a core strategic project for the organisation, confronting the future volunteer and service delivery challenges facing the movement. Each of these initiatives exists because Chris saw the need, argued for it and carried it.
>
> Significant. This is not the administration of an existing system but the transformation of it. Every Surf Rescue Certificate, Bronze Medallion and Silver Medallion candidate in Australia now trains through models and manuals Chris built or rebuilt, reforms that continue to shape the development of thousands of new members every year, and every club's resuscitation practice is being lifted by an initiative he led. Through twelve years on the National Meritorious Awards Committee (2013-2025), seven as Chair (2017-2024), he also shaped how SLSA recognises its own members, overseeing the Lifesaver of the Year and Volunteer of the Year awards and their judging panels, leading the 2021 review of the lifesaving award criteria and introducing the Youth Surf Life Saver of the Year award so that the next generation of standouts is recognised as he once was.
>
> Sustained. His national service began at the 2006 SLSA Youth Development Forum, twenty years ago, and has never stopped. He has been a national Trainer, Assessor and Facilitator since 2007, piloted the Silver Medallion Aquatic Rescue in 2011, and served fourteen consecutive years on the Lifesaving Members Advisory Committee (2012-2025) with nine as National Chair. There is no gap in this record. Every season for two decades, Chris has been doing the work.
>
> Conspicuous. He was named SLSA Australian Surf Lifesaver of the Year in 2011/12, the youngest ever recipient and the only Tasmanian recipient. His efforts have earned the praise of even his harshest critics, and the sheer volume and quality of his output is so far beyond what anyone expects of a volunteer that members around the country routinely assume he is paid staff. He is not, and never has been. Twenty years of that record, given freely, is the definition of conspicuous service.
